proposal: Add a private persistence-change side channel while keeping the root state update
source_fact: useBlockSync currently subscribes to the block-editor store with registry.subscribe( listener, blockEditorStore ) and reads isLastBlockChangePersistent().
what_it_solves: Creates a migration seam for the known in-tree semantic consumer and lets tests prove that the onInput to onChange handoff still works.
what_it_does_not_solve: Does not reduce ordinary useSelect fanout because MARK_LAST_CHANGE_AS_PERSISTENT still changes blocks.isPersistentChange and therefore the block-editor root state.
required_validation: useBlockSync tests for non-persistent onInput, persistent onChange, persistence flip after a previous block change with no block-array identity change, selection reporting, controlled inner blocks, fresh callbacks, and unmount cleanup.
decision: Useful prototype seam, not a performance win by itself.

proposal: Move useBlockSync to the side channel and stop changing the block-editor root for persistence-only markers
source_fact: The hot marker action changes only blocks.isPersistentChange; audited hot selectors do not read that branch.
what_it_solves: Would preserve the known in-tree useBlockSync path and avoid waking thousands of ordinary block-editor useSelect subscribers for persistence-only markers.
what_it_does_not_solve: Breaks public subscription semantics for isLastBlockChangePersistent consumers because useSelect and registry.subscribe are store-level, not selector-level.
required_validation: Compatibility decision for public selector consumers; benchmark showing marker-only rootSubscribe/useSelect listener counts fall while useBlockSync still emits the same onChange/onInput sequence.
decision: Blocked for a production performance change until the public selector contract is resolved.

proposal: Keep the selector value correct from an external persistence slot
source_fact: The public selector is currently a pure state selector returning state.blocks.isPersistentChange.
what_it_solves: Could make imperative select( blockEditorStore ).isLastBlockChangePersistent() return the latest value if the selector reads a separate slot.
what_it_does_not_solve: Would not notify existing useSelect or store subscribers when only that external slot changes, and would weaken the state-selector contract.
required_validation: Data-layer review before considering this; tests for direct select are not enough.
decision: Do not use as the compatibility answer.

proposal: Add selector-aware or branch-aware subscriptions to @wordpress/data
source_fact: useSelect records active store names and invalidates on any subscribed store change; the Redux wrapper calls every listener on root identity change.
what_it_solves: Could preserve public isLastBlockChangePersistent useSelect notifications while letting unrelated block-editor selectors skip persistence-only changes.
what_it_does_not_solve: Broad data-layer contract change with dynamic selector dependencies, cross-store reads, conditional selectors, and plugin compatibility risk.
required_validation: Separate data-layer research prototype with selector dependency tests before applying to block-editor persistence.
decision: Only complete compatibility route found, but not a near-term typing benchmark patch.

proposal: Do local selector guards before store partitioning
source_fact: Pattern override has a clear selected-only split; provider and inner-blocks have local invalidation prototypes; none changes public data subscription semantics.
what_it_solves: Reduces a source-feasible local envelope before taking on store-level compatibility risk.
what_it_does_not_solve: Does not remove the full persistence-marker fanout.
required_validation: Patch and measure pattern override first, then validate provider and inner-block invalidation keys.
